  • 3
    Lesson 1.5: The official quickstart and recovery orderFrom the web

    The docs quickstart says to get plain chat working first, then add the next layer (gateway, tools, skills, a Docker sandbox). Hermes needs a model with at least 64K tokens of context. Secrets go in ~/.hermes/.env and other settings in ~/.hermes/config.yaml.

    1. Pick a provider with: hermes model
    2. Start a chat with: hermes --tui
    3. Check sessions resume with: hermes -c
    4. Only then run: hermes gateway setup
    5. If something breaks, go in this order: hermes doctor, hermes model, hermes setup, hermes sessions list, hermes --continue, hermes gateway status
    Hermes Agent
    Hermes docs: Quickstart web
  • 4
    Lesson 2: Soul, memory and skills

    The courses teach the mental model: a SOUL.md persona file, built-in memory files (USER.md, MEMORY.md) for facts, and skills for repeatable procedures kept separate from facts. Sharbel A. and Jack Roberts lay this out; the 3-hour course builds self-made skills on top.

    1. Write a SOUL.md so the agent knows its role
    2. Keep facts in memory files and procedures in skills
    3. Save a job the agent does well as a skill so it reuses it
    SOUL.mdMEMORY.md and USER.mdSelf-written skills from SOPsHermes /learn

    For you: Each of your seven agents keeps its own lane this way.

    Learn 95% of Hermes Agent in 31 Minutes Sharbel A.HERMES AGENT FULL COURSE 3 HOURS: Build & Sell (2026) Samin YasarEvery Hermes Concept explained for Normal People Jack Roberts
  • 5
    Lesson 2.5: How Hermes memory really worksFrom the web

    Built-in memory is two small files in ~/.hermes/memories/: MEMORY.md (the agent's notes, 2,200 characters) and USER.md (your profile, 1,375 characters). They load as a frozen snapshot at session start, so a change shows only in the next session. Memory does not auto-compact: when full, the agent must tidy it before writing more. Writes are scanned for injection and leaked credentials.

    1. Turn on write approval in config.yaml (memory: write_approval: true) to review each write
    2. Review staged writes with /memory pending, then /memory approve <id> or /memory reject <id>
    3. Start a fresh session with /new so new memory loads

    For you: Write approval suits Mantis and any agent that touches private notes.

    Watch out: External memory plugins (Honcho, Mem0 and others) run alongside built-in memory; have Sentinel review any before install.

    Hermes docs: Memory web
  • 6
    Lesson 2.6: Skills the official wayFrom the web

    A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file (YAML front matter, then instructions), stored in ~/.hermes/skills/. Every hub install passes a built-in scanner for data theft, prompt injection and destructive commands, and gets a trust level: builtin, official, trusted or community. A 'dangerous' verdict can never be forced through.

    1. Look before you install: hermes skills inspect <name>
    2. Check installed skills: hermes skills audit
    3. Set skills.write_approval: true so agent-made skills wait for review
    Hermes Agent

    For you: This is the gate Sentinel should sit behind before you say yes to any skill.

    Watch out: The scanner helps but does not replace a human read; the videos still say to read skills from unknown authors line by line.

    Hermes docs: Skills web

    Lesson 3: Cron jobs and a first real job

    The most-named Hermes feature. Sharbel A.'s classic is a morning cron that asks your number-one priority and starts work; Metics Media shows the agent writing its own watch-and-report skill and schedule.

    1. Create a cron job for one recurring task
    2. Have it message you with a result, not just run silently
    3. Add approval gates so it asks before spending or sending
    Hermes cron jobsMorning brief cronApproval gates

Security for agents 7, in order

  • 1
    Lesson 0: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM apps (2025)From the web

    OWASP's standard list of the ten biggest risks in apps built on language models: LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure, LLM03 Supply Chain, LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning, LLM05 Improper Output Handling, LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM07 System Prompt Leakage, LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses, LLM09 Misinformation, LLM10 Unbounded Consumption (runaway cost or resource use).

    For you: Sentinel's reviews can use these ten as a checklist.

    OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications web
  • 2
    Lesson 0.5: The OWASP Top 10 for agents (2026)From the web

    Published 9 Dec 2025, this list is about agents that act: ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack, ASI02 Tool Misuse, ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse, ASI04 Agentic Supply Chain (bad MCP servers, connectors, prompts), ASI05 Unexpected Code Execution, ASI06 Memory and Context Poisoning, ASI07 Insecure Inter-Agent Communication, ASI08 Cascading Failures, ASI09 Human-Agent Trust Exploitation, ASI10 Rogue Agents.

    For you: ASI06 and ASI07 map straight onto shared vault memory and agents messaging each other in Discord.

    OWASP: Top 10 for Agentic Applications announcement webCycode summary of ASI01 to ASI10 web
  • 3
    Lesson 1: Harden the server first

    Metics Media's VPS tutorials: a non-root sudo user, SSH keys (ed25519), a firewall (UFW) allowing only SSH, 80 and 443, and backups on from day one. Dokploy or Coolify-style panels sit on top.

    1. Make a non-root sudo user
    2. Set up SSH keys and disable password login
    3. Open only the ports you need with UFW
    4. Turn on snapshots or backups
    Ubuntu server hardeningHostinger VPSLet's Encrypt

    For you: Your VPS runs Coolify; the same hardening rules apply.

    Hostinger VPS Tutorial 2026: Step-by-Step Guide for Beginners Metics MediaHow to Deploy a Web App to a VPS (2026) - Dokploy Metics Media
  • 4
    Lesson 1.5: Lock down Hermes itselfFrom the web

    The Hermes security docs: risky shell commands go through approvals (mode smart by default, or manual, or off), a hard blocklist always refuses things like disk wipes, and timed-out approvals are denied. Chat gateways deny everyone unless you set an allowlist. Writes to SSH keys and secret stores are blocked.

    1. Set explicit allowlists; never set GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true
    2. Protect the secrets file: chmod 600 ~/.hermes/.env
    3. Review approval history with: hermes approvals suggest (it never changes anything by itself)
    4. Run the gateway as a non-root user in a container, and run hermes update regularly
    Hermes Agent

    Watch out: The docs say the deny rules reduce accidents but do not sandbox a hostile agent; approvals off or YOLO mode removes most prompts.

    Hermes docs: Security web

Prompting well 4, in order

  • 1
    Lesson 1: Be clear, and say whyFrom the web

    Anthropic's guide: treat Claude like a brilliant new employee with no context. Test: show the prompt to a colleague; if they would be confused, Claude will be too. Give the reason behind a rule, for example 'this will be read aloud', instead of a bare 'NEVER do X'.

    For you: Useful when you write SOUL files and skills for the agents.

    Claude docs: Be clear and direct web
  • 2
    Lesson 2: Show 3 to 5 examplesFrom the web

    Examples steer format and tone better than description. Use 3 to 5 that are relevant and varied (include edge cases), and wrap each in <example> tags, inside <examples>, so Claude does not mix them up with instructions. You can ask Claude to check your examples or write more.

    Claude docs: Using examples web
  • 3
    Lesson 3: Label the parts with XML tagsFrom the web

    Put instructions, context and input in their own tags, such as <instructions>, <context> and <input>. For long documents, put the documents first and the question last, and ask Claude to quote the relevant parts before answering.

    Claude docs: Use XML tags web
  • 4
    Lesson 4: Say what to do, and be explicit about actionFrom the web

    Tell Claude what to do, not what to avoid: 'write in flowing paragraphs' works better than 'don't use markdown'. 'Can you suggest changes?' may get only suggestions; 'Change this function' gets edits.

    Claude docs: Be clear and direct web

  • Hermes dashboard login rules, per its docsFrom the web

    hermes dashboard runs on 127.0.0.1:9119 with no login by default. If you bind it to any other address, it refuses to start until a login is set up: username and password (for trusted networks or VPN only), Nous Portal OAuth (recommended for internet-facing), or your own OIDC such as authentik. The docs recommend keeping it on loopback and reaching it by SSH tunnel or Tailscale.

    1. Keep the dashboard bound to 127.0.0.1.
    2. Reach it over an SSH tunnel or Tailscale.
    3. Behind a reverse proxy, set dashboard.public_url and a narrow dashboard.trusted_proxies list.
    4. Check the gate with the docs' curl call to /api/status.
    Hermes web dashboardTailscale

    Watch out: The Kanban docs say plugin routes are not authenticated, so --host 0.0.0.0 exposes the board.

    Hermes web dashboard docs web

    On a Hostinger VPS the Hermes dashboard can be put behind HTTPS with a Traefik option. It shows sessions, models, cron, skills, keys, channels and logs, and the system page can stop, start or restart the gateway.

    Hermes web dashboardHostinger VPSTraefikLet's Encrypt

  • hermes-webui: turn the password onFrom the web

    nesquena's Hermes WebUI binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and its password is off by default. You turn it on with HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD or in Settings; passkeys and OIDC login are also supported.   • Authelia: a login gate for the reverse proxyFrom the web

    A 2FA and single sign-on server that works as an add-on to your reverse proxy. It has second factors such as one-time codes, security keys and passkeys, and Duo push, plus lockout after too many tries. Its docs list Traefik, Caddy, NGINX and others as supported proxies.

    AutheliaTraefik

  • authentik: your own single sign-onFrom the web

    A self-hosted identity provider (one login for many apps). It speaks OAuth2/OIDC, SAML, LDAP and RADIUS. Core is MIT, with a separate paid enterprise part. Installs with Docker Compose for small setups. About 26.1k stars.

    authentik

    For you: Homarr, Hermes's dashboard and hermes-webui can all use OIDC, so one authentik login could cover them. It is in Coolify's one-click list.

    Watch out: One more server to secure and back up; worth it only once several apps need logins.

    goauthentik/authentik on GitHub webauthentik website web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Cloudflare Access in front of a tunnelFrom the web

    Access puts a login wall in front of a self-hosted app on a public name. Every app is deny by default; only people matching an Allow policy get in, through a login provider you pick (for example Google or GitHub) and optional MFA. The app is connected through a Cloudflare Tunnel.

    1. Create the Access application and its Allow policy first.
    2. Then add the tunnel route, so the app is never open for a moment.
    3. Make the origin reject requests that skip Access (cloudflared can check the Access token).
    Cloudflare Tunnel

    For you: Only for a page that must be reached without Tailscale; donts.json says dashboards stay off the open internet.

    Watch out: Order matters: a tunnel without the Access app first is open to anyone with the link.

    Cloudflare: publish a self-hosted app web
  • Harden the server

    Metics Media's VPS basics: a non-root sudo user, SSH keys only, and a UFW firewall that allows only SSH, 80 and 443. Change app defaults on day one; Umami ships with the login admin/umami.

    1. Create a sudo user and stop using root.
    2. Use SSH keys and turn off password logins.
    3. Allow only the ports you need in the firewall.
    4. Change every default login straight away.
    5. Switch on backups and snapshots.
    Ubuntu server hardeningUmamiDokploy

  • Tailscale Serve, per Tailscale's docsFrom the web

    Serve shares a local web app with the devices on your own tailnet (your private Tailscale network) only. Tailscale gives it an HTTPS certificate for its tailnet name. Funnel is the different command that makes it public on the internet.

    1. Turn on HTTPS for the tailnet (the interactive flow does this for you).
    2. Run the docs' example form: tailscale serve 3000 (shares the app on port 3000).
    3. Run tailscale serve --help for more examples.
    TailscaleTailscale Serve

    Watch out: Use Serve, not Funnel, for intranet pages; Funnel is public.

  • Checkmk: one page that watches everything

    NetworkChuck installs the free Checkmk community edition on a VM in under five minutes and monitors Linux servers, network gear, Docker containers, Proxmox VMs, websites and a Windows PC. Data is collected every minute and kept for up to four years, with default good and bad thresholds. Every change must be activated, a bit like committing code.

PProcesses for setting stuff up

Install and configure the tools in the videos, in order, with a check at the end of each. Where it touches Chris's own stack, a fit line says what changes.

From your videos: 22 procedures from 37 of the 105 videos. Hermes, VPS hardening, Ollama and MCP have full steps; no video walks through Coolify, Tailscale or n8n self-hosting. Plus 10 entries from the web (marked From the web) and web-sourced steps for the Tailscale and n8n starter-kit entries, filling the Coolify, Tailscale, n8n, Hermes install and update, Obsidian Git, OpenRouter key and SSH gaps.

Coolify 2, A to Z

  • Deploy a first app in CoolifyFrom the web

    Coolify's own first-app guide uses a ready-made Docker image (nginx), so there is no code or build to set up. It is a safe way to check a new server works end to end.

    1. Click New Project, give it a name and click Continue.
    2. Open the project and click Create New Resource.
    3. Choose Docker Image and enter nginx:alpine
    4. Set Ports Exposes to 80.
    5. Keep the test domain Coolify makes (an sslip.io address), or point your own domain's DNS at the server and replace it.
    6. Click Deploy and wait.
    7. Open the app's address and check the Nginx welcome page loads.
    Docker

    For you: Matches Chris's rule for changes: Stop, then Deploy, not Restart. Delete nothing afterwards; archive per his rule.

    Watch out: A test app on a public domain is public. Remove or stop it when done, or keep it on Tailscale only.

    Coolify docs: Deploy your first app web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Install Coolify on a serverFrom the web

    Coolify is a self-hosted control panel for apps and services. It needs Linux (Ubuntu LTS is fine; for non-LTS Ubuntu use the manual install), 2 CPU cores, 2 GB RAM and 10 GB free disk, on amd64 or arm64. No video walks through it; these steps are from Coolify's docs.

    1. Log in to the server over SSH as root or a sudo user.
    2. Run: curl -fsSL https://cdn.coollabs.io/coolify/install.sh | bash
    3. Wait for the installer to finish; it prints the next steps.
    4. Open http://<server-ip>:8000 in your browser.
    5. Create the admin account straight away.
    6. Back up /data/coolify/source/.env somewhere safe; it holds the secrets needed to restore Coolify.
    Docker

    For you: Chris already runs Coolify on agent86.cloud; this is for a rebuild or a second server. Keep the .env backup out of the vault and out of Discord.

    Watch out: Coolify warns that whoever reaches the sign-up page first becomes admin with root access to the server, so do step 5 at once.

    Coolify docs: Installation web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Connect a chat channel (Telegram by QR)

    Telegram has a QR flow in the Hermes dashboard. Other channels (Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, email) are listed, and Tina Huang connects them by asking Hermes to help.

    1. Have your phone ready with Telegram installed; the QR code expires after about three minutes.
    2. In Channels, choose Telegram and click Create with QR. Scan it and create the bot.
    3. Click Save and Restart in the dashboard. If the gateway says it is not running, click Restart Gateway.
    4. Refresh until Telegram shows 'connected', then press Start in Telegram and send a message.
    5. Type /sethome so cron results and alerts land in that chat.
    6. For another app, start a session and ask: 'Help me connect to Discord' (or WhatsApp, and so on).
    7. Check: only you get replies (you are on the allow list), and a test cron delivers to the home channel.
    TelegramDiscordHermes gateways

  • Connect a model provider

    Hermes needs a model before it can think. The videos show three ways in: the dashboard Keys page, the hermes model command, or a subscription login.

    1. OpenRouter route: make an account, copy the API key into a password manager, add credit (Metics Media starts with 5 dollars) and set a limit on the key.
    2. In the Hermes dashboard open Keys, expand OpenRouter, click Set, paste the key and Save.
    3. Open Models, find main model, click Change, pick a model, Switch, then Reload.
    4. Terminal route: run hermes model, pick a provider, and follow the login (a ChatGPT/Codex plan uses a device code you paste back).
    5. Add a second, cheaper provider the same way and give it the auxiliary tasks.
    6. Check: send hello in Chat; the 'no provider' error is gone and it replies. Watch spend on OpenRouter's Activity page.

    For you: Chris uses OpenRouter with Claude Haiku: one key per agent, each with its own limit. Keys never go into Discord.

    Watch out: If ChatGPT login fails, Python Simplified says to enable device code authorisation in ChatGPT's security settings.

  • Install a skill safely

    Several videos install skills by pasting a GitHub link into the agent. Others say to review first. This order puts the review before the install.

    1. Check whether Hermes already has it built in (Capabilities or Skills page).
    2. Read the skill file yourself or have Sentinel read it line by line; Nuno Tavares asks Claude or Codex to security-scan the repo URL first.
    3. Optionally scan it with a tool shown in the videos (Nvidia's Skill Inspector).
    4. Check its size: Dubibubi says a good skill stays under 15 KB.
    5. Then give the agent the link and say 'install this skill'.
    6. Check: it appears in the skills list, and one test run behaves as expected.
    Skills HubSkill Inspector (Nvidia)Skill directories (SkillsMP, SkillHub, ClawHub)

    For you: Chris's rule: nothing is installed without Sentinel's review and his yes.

  • Install Hermes from the official scriptFrom the web

    Hermes's own docs give one command for Linux, macOS and WSL2, one for Windows, and desktop app bundles for Mac (Apple Silicon only; Intel Macs are not supported) and Windows. The script needs Git, curl, tar and SHA-256 tools.

    1. Linux, Mac or WSL2: curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
    2. Windows (PowerShell): iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)
    3. Reload your shell: source ~/.bashrc (or source ~/.zshrc on a Mac).
    4. Start it: hermes. The installer also runs setup unless you passed --non-interactive.
    5. Change things later with hermes model, hermes tools, hermes gateway setup, or hermes setup (the full wizard).
    6. Check: hermes doctor reports what is missing and how to fix it.

  • Update Hermes safelyFrom the web

    hermes update pulls the latest stable release, backs up key files first, checks the key startup files compile (and rolls back if not), and restarts running gateways. Image- or package-managed installs (such as Docker) are different: Hermes reports the outside update command instead.

    1. Preview first: hermes update --check (are you behind?) and hermes update --plan (what will restart).
    2. Update: hermes update. By default it saves a quick snapshot of config.yaml, .env, auth.json, pairing data and cron jobs.
    3. If it asks about new settings, answer, or later run hermes config check then hermes config migrate.
    4. Check afterwards: hermes --version, hermes doctor and hermes gateway status.
    5. Docker or other image installs: hermes update --plan reports the outside update command to use instead; pull the new image, then recreate the container with the same data folder.
    hermes doctorhermes gateway restart

    For you: If Chris's Hermes runs from the Docker image under Coolify, the Docker route applies; in Coolify that means Stop, then Deploy (his standing rule).

    Watch out: Rolling back is manual: an older release cannot read a state.db the new one has written, so keep the snapshot. Chats made after the update are not in it.

Server (VPS) 4, A to Z

  • Harden a new Ubuntu VPS

    Metics Media's beginner procedure on a plain Ubuntu LTS server: update, make a normal admin user, log in with an SSH key, and turn on a firewall. Every command below is read out in the video.

    1. In the provider's browser terminal: apt update && apt upgrade -y
    2. Make a user: adduser username (press Enter through the optional fields, then Y).
    3. Give it admin rights: usermod -aG sudo username
    4. Check: id username should list sudo. Switch to it: su - username
    5. On your own computer: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "a note" and copy the contents of the .pub file.
    6. Back on the server as the new user: mkdir -p ~/.ssh then nano ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, paste the key, save with Ctrl O, Enter, Ctrl X.
    7. Lock it down: chmod 700 ~/.ssh and chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
    8. From your computer: ssh username@your-server-ip and type yes to trust it. If it closes, run sudo systemctl restart ssh on the server and try again.
    9. Firewall: sudo ufw status, then sudo ufw allow OpenSSH, sudo ufw allow 80/tcp, sudo ufw allow 443/tcp, then sudo ufw enable
    10. Reboot to apply everything: sudo reboot
    11. Check afterwards: you can log in with the key, sudo ufw status lists only SSH, 80 and 443, and backups are on.
    Hostinger VPS

    For you: Chris's VPS already runs Coolify: before enabling a firewall, list the ports Coolify and its apps need, or you can lock services out. Sentinel should review firewall changes.

    Watch out: The video does not show turning off root or password login; do not assume it is done.

    Hostinger VPS Tutorial 2026: Step-by-Step Guide for Beginners Metics Media
  • Know which Coolify ports to allow before turning on a firewallFrom the web

    Coolify's firewall page lists six ports for a server running Coolify itself. Once the dashboard works through a domain, the three direct-access ports can be closed, because everything then goes through 80 and 443.

    1. 22/tcp: SSH (or your own SSH port). Never remove this rule while setting up the firewall.
    2. 80/tcp: web traffic and making HTTPS certificates through Coolify's proxy.
    3. 443/tcp: HTTPS through Coolify's proxy.
    4. 8000/tcp: dashboard by IP address. 6001/tcp: live dashboard updates. 6002/tcp: web terminal.
    5. Once the dashboard opens on its domain, close public access to 8000, 6001 and 6002.
    6. Open any other port only when an app needs it (for example a public database port or GitHub webhooks).
    Hostinger VPS

    For you: Answers the 'list the ports first' note on 'Harden a new Ubuntu VPS'. Chris's dashboard is already on coolify.agent86.cloud, so 8000, 6001 and 6002 should not need to be public.

    Watch out: Coolify: 'Do not open ports that your server does not use.'

    Coolify docs: Firewall web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Turn off root login and password login for SSHFrom the web

    The video procedure stops before this. Ubuntu's docs say a settings file in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ wins over the main file, because SSH uses the first value it reads. Tecmint names the three lines to set and warns that cloud images can ship a file that turns passwords back on.

    1. First make sure you can already log in with your SSH key as a normal sudo user.
    2. Keep that SSH window open the whole time; open a second one for testing.
    3. Back up the original: copy /etc/ssh/sshd_config somewhere safe.
    4. Make a new file /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-hardening.conf (the 00 makes it load before cloud files such as 50-cloud-init.conf).
    5. Put three lines in it: PermitRootLogin no, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
    6. Check the settings: sudo sshd -t (no output means no errors).
    7. Apply: sudo systemctl restart ssh.service
    8. In the second window, log in with your key. Only close the first window once this works.
    Hostinger VPS

    For you: Fixes the gap in 'Harden a new Ubuntu VPS'. Coolify connects to its own server over SSH, so check Coolify still shows the server as reachable afterwards; Sentinel should review first.

    Watch out: Ubuntu's docs: a mistake here can lock you out of a server you only reach by SSH. Keep Hostinger's browser terminal as a way back in.

    Ubuntu Server docs: OpenSSH server webTecmint: SSH hardening tips on Ubuntu servers web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • How each Artcraft app holds up (AI Samson's test)

    Replaces: Adobe Creative Cloud (he pays about $70 a month). A 'clean room' build: no Adobe code; it was written by Claude in Rust from public file specs and how the apps behave. PhotoCraft is 80 MB against Photoshop's 6.4 GB, and FilmCraft is 90 MB against Premiere's 6.8 GB. PhotoCraft opens layered PSD files. VectorCraft has 89 of Illustrator's 92 tools and works with SVG and PDF. FilmCraft cannot open Premiere projects but imports timelines by XML. EffectCraft runs After Effects scripts but cannot open .aep files.

    For you: Fine for learning and personal work, he says; not yet for paid client deadlines.

    Watch out: Artcraft itself lists the gaps: generative AI features, 15 missing tools, typography depth and plugin support. VectorCraft struggles with .ai files and logo tracing. Slow on older Macs. It makes money by selling credits for AI models.

TTutorials

Longer walk-throughs that follow one video from start to finish: what you will build, the steps in the video's order, and what you end up with.

From your videos: 14 tutorials, one per video, from 14 of the 105 videos. 10 were checked against full transcripts; 4 (marked) follow the notes only. Most of the 105 are news, tool lists or opinion, not step-by-step builds. Plus 7 free official tutorials from the web (marked From the web).

Build a Hermes agent from zero 4, A to Z

  • Hermes fundamentals on a home machine (Tina Huang)

    What you will build: a desktop-app Hermes with a provider, a self-made skill, cron jobs, four tiers of memory (files, session search, Honcho, an Obsidian vault) and a free local model.

    1. Choose hardware: a dedicated machine, a VPS, an old laptop wiped clean, or your own computer inside Docker.
    2. Download the desktop app from the Hermes site (or use the terminal installer).
    3. Add a provider under Models > Edit models > Add provider (she suggests Nous Portal if you have none).
    4. Tell it about yourself and ask it to remember; see the user.md and memory.md files in the .hermes folder.
    5. Try built-in tools (web search), connect a chat app by asking 'Help me connect to Telegram', and add an MCP by asking for it.
    6. Do a task, then say 'Make this into a skill' and call it later with a slash.
    7. Set cron jobs such as a nightly brief or a nightly health check.
    8. Ask 'Help me set up Honcho' for deeper memory and check it with hermes honcho status.
    9. Create an Obsidian vault and ask Hermes to connect it; save research there with the Obsidian skill.
    10. Install Ollama and use its launch tab (or ask Hermes) to run a local model.
    11. Optional: build with several agents from Discord and the Kanban board.
    Hermes desktop appNous PortalHonchoObsidianOllamallama.cppQwen 3.6 35B A3BNotebookLM MCPHermes Kanban board

    For you: Her four memory tiers map well onto Chris's vault plus the planned Qdrant index for Cerebra.

    Watch out: She runs a local Qwen 3.6 35B on a 64 GB Mac Studio; smaller machines need smaller models.

    Hermes Agent Fundamentals In 29 Minutes Tina Huang
  • Hermes on a small server, with phone and desktop (Metics Media)

    What you will build: a Hermes agent that runs all day on a rented server, thinks with a cheap OpenRouter model, talks to you on Telegram, and also opens on your Mac through the desktop app. About 30 minutes, no code.

    1. Pick a Hostinger KVM 1 plan, untick the pre-checked 'Ready to Use AI' add-on, and pay (the coupon needs 12 months or more).
    2. In the deploy form keep the username 'Hermes', copy the admin password into a password manager, and click Deploy.
    3. Wait for 'running' with a green check, click Open and sign in to the web dashboard.

Build automations and connectors 3, A to Z

  • A mini research agent in n8n (AI Foundations)

    What you will build: an n8n workflow that takes a topic from a form, writes five search queries, researches them through OpenRouter, and saves the result to an Airtable record.

    1. Learn the three principles first: fix the research structure up front, keep a 'rotating' database you write to as you go, and split research into one task per section.
    2. Sketch the flow: input, query refiner, style guide, research manager, research loop, final PDF.
    3. In n8n, start with an 'On form submission' trigger with one text field for the topic.
    4. Add an agent node as the query refiner, connect an OpenAI chat model, and paste a prompt asking for five search queries.
    5. Add a Structured Output Parser with the JSON shape so the output is consistent; test it.
    6. In Airtable, create a base and table (topic name, content), and a token with read, write and schema-read scopes for that base.
    7. Add an Airtable 'create record' node that saves the topic.
    8. Add an HTTP Request to OpenRouter with your key as a Bearer token, a system message and the topic plus five queries in the JSON body (he used Perplexity Sonar).
    9. Split out the message, merge it with the Airtable record ID, then aggregate into one item.
    10. Add an Airtable 'update record' node to write the research into the content field, and test the whole flow.
    n8nAirtableOpenRouterPerplexity Sonar tool

  • Your first MCP server and client in Python (KodeKloud)

    What you will build: a flight-booking MCP server with resources, tools and prompts, connected to a coding assistant, plus a simple client.

    1. Learn why: an agent needs tools to act, and MCP is a standard way to describe those tools.
    2. Learn the parts: the server offers tools, resources and prompts; messages use JSON-RPC 2.0; transport is standard IO or HTTP.
    3. Connect an existing server: in the assistant's MCP settings, edit the project MCP file with the command uv and the arguments run python server.py, then refresh and look for a green status.
    4. Approve the first tool call and check the answer.
    5. Build your own: uv init a project, cd into it, and uv add the MCP package.
    6. In server.py, use FastMCP and mark functions with the resource, tool and prompt decorators.
    7. Run it with standard IO, or HTTP with a host and port.
    8. Test it in the MCP Inspector web page before writing a client.
    9. Write a client that lists tools, calls one, reads a resource and gets prompts.
    10. Learn the client-side extras: roots (allowed folders), sampling (server asks the client's model) and elicitation (server asks the user).
    Model Context ProtocolFastMCPMCP InspectorRoo Code

PreviousHomeNext

UUncensored AI

What the videos say about 'uncensored' open models: models whose safety training has been loosened or stripped, run on your own machine so nothing is filtered and nothing leaves your computer. This tab stays factual and spells out the risks.

From your videos: Only two of the 105 videos are mainly about this: 'Private & UNCENSORED Local AI Model' and 'Build Your Own UNCENSORED AI Running Completely Offline'; a handful more touch local models in passing, and none explains how a model is made uncensored. Plus 10 entries from the web to fill gaps (marked From the web): abliteration and the research behind it, Dolphin and abliterated families, malware in model files, licences, Hugging Face rules and Canadian law.

Known families and where they are shared 2, A to Z

  • Abliterated copies on Hugging FaceFrom the web

    Many abliterated models are published by individual uploaders, for example huihui-ai's abliterated Qwen builds. One such card (Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated) says safety filtering 'has been significantly reduced', recommends research or controlled use only, not production or public-facing commercial apps, and says the uploader bears no responsibility.

    Hugging Face

    Watch out: No benchmarks are given on that card. An uploader's disclaimer means the risk is yours.

    huihui-ai: Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Dolphin: the best-known uncensored familyFrom the web

    Dolphin 3.0 was curated and trained by Eric Hartford, Ben Gitter, BlouseJury and Cognitive Computations. Dolphin 3.0 is built on Meta's Llama 3.1 8B under the Llama 3.1 licence. Its card tells the operator 'You are the one who decides the guidelines', and that 'you are the creator and originator of any content you generate with Dolphin.'

    OllamaHugging Face

    Watch out: Older Dolphin builds on Ollama (dolphin-mixtral, about 26 GB for 8x7b) are Apache 2.0 but over a year old; the card's message is that all responsibility sits with you.

    Dolphin 3.0 Llama 3.1 8B model card webOllama: dolphin-mixtral web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

The risks, said plainly 9, A to Z

  • Canadian law on AI-made sexual imagesFrom the web

    Creating or possessing sexual images of children is illegal in Canada whether photographed or AI-generated. Bill C-16, the Protecting Victims Act, received Royal Assent on 18 June 2026: it extends the ban on sharing intimate images without consent to sexual deepfakes, makes threatening to share them an offence, and raises the maximum penalty to 10 years.

    Watch out: Running a model offline changes nothing legally; the law is about what is made and shared. Information only, not legal advice.

    Justice Canada: Protecting Victims Act (Bill C-16) webBetaKit: gaps in Canada's deepfake laws (Jan 2026) web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Hugging Face's own content rulesFrom the web

    Hugging Face's content policy (effective 10 April 2025) bans non-consensual sexual content, any sexual content involving minors, malware, hate and harassment, and fraud. Uploaders must take steps to reduce the risk their models are used to make child sexual exploitation or terror material.

    Watch out: A model being hosted there does not mean it was vetted.

    Hugging Face Content Policy web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Legal and ethical caution

    An uncensored model will produce content a hosted model blocks, which can include unsafe, unlawful or harmful material. Running one offline does not make the output safe to act on or to share, and you remain responsible for how it is used.

    Build Your Own UNCENSORED AI Running Completely Offline channel unknown
  • Measured: abliteration costs qualityFrom the web

    In Labonne's test, the abliterated Daredevil-8B scored lower than its source model on every benchmark he ran. A further training pass (DPO, a preference-tuning method) won back most of the loss, but not on GSM8K, a maths benchmark.

    For you: Backs up the existing point that removing safety also removes a quality guard.

    Hugging Face blog: Uncensor any LLM with abliteration (Jun 2024) web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Model files can carry malwareFrom the web

    In February 2024 JFrog found about 100 malicious models on Hugging Face. One PyTorch model used Python's pickle format so that simply loading it opened a reverse shell to an outside server. Hugging Face flags unsafe pickle files but, at the time, did not block downloads (it removed that model after reports).

    For you: Exactly why Sentinel reviews before anything is installed.

    Watch out: Prefer the safer safetensors format and named uploaders; never load a pickle file from an unknown account.

    JFrog: malicious Hugging Face models with silent backdoor web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Removing safety training also removes a quality guard

    Stripping refusals does not only unlock blocked topics; it can make a model more willing to give confident, wrong or harmful answers, because the same training that made it refuse also curbed bad output. Treat anything it says as unverified.

    For you: Clashes with your 'always give me facts, check first' rule: an uncensored model is less trustworthy, not more.

    Private & UNCENSORED Local AI Model | No Filter, No Internet JarvesExplainsBuild Your Own UNCENSORED AI Running Completely Offline channel unknown
  • The original licence still applies to edited copiesFrom the web

    Editing a model does not cancel its licence. Google's Gemma Terms cover 'Model Derivatives', including modified Gemma, and require passing the Prohibited Use Policy on to anyone you share it with. Gemma 4 has its own separate licence. Meta's Llama policy bars using Llama to break the law or risk bodily harm.

    Watch out: Removing refusals does not remove your obligations under the licence.

    Gemma Terms of Use (updated 1 Apr 2026) webMeta Llama Acceptable Use Policy web
  • Unknown weights from unknown sources

    Both videos find models by searching one word and name no author or repo. Downloading edited model weights from an unnamed source is the same trust problem as installing an unread skill, which your donts list warns against.

    Watch out: Your rule is Sentinel reads anything before it is installed and you prefer named authors; neither video gives one.

    Private & UNCENSORED Local AI Model | No Filter, No Internet JarvesExplainsBuild Your Own UNCENSORED AI Running Completely Offline channel unknown
  • Where this could sit, if at all

    If there is any case for a private local model in your setup it is privacy, not removing safety. A standard local model (plain Gemma 4 or Qwen through Ollama or LM Studio) gives the offline, private benefit without stripping the safety training.

    OllamaLM StudioGemma 4

    For you: A safer middle path for Mantis's private lane than an uncensored build.

    Private & UNCENSORED Local AI Model | No Filter, No Internet JarvesExplainsBuild Your Own UNCENSORED AI Running Completely Offline channel unknown

What 'uncensored' means here 5, A to Z

  • Abliteration versus fine-tuningFrom the web

    Fine-tuning trains a model further on new examples to change its behaviour. Abliteration skips training and edits the weights once. Dolphin-style 'uncensored' models use the fine-tuning route instead: trained on data meant to make the model follow the operator's system prompt rather than the maker's rules.

    Watch out: Either way, the result is a changed copy of someone else's model, made by a third party.

    Hugging Face blog: Uncensor any LLM with abliteration (Jun 2024) webDolphin 3.0 Llama 3.1 8B model card web
  • The plain idea

    A normal chat model is trained to refuse some requests. An 'uncensored' model has had that refusal behaviour loosened or removed, so it answers things the standard version would block. JarvesExplains demonstrates this by asking the same question to a normal Gemma 4 (it refuses) and an uncensored Gemma 4 (it answers), both running locally. The videos also use the word 'abliterated' for this kind of edited model.

    Watch out: The videos show the difference but never explain how the change is made, and name no safe, vetted source for these edited weights.

    Private & UNCENSORED Local AI Model | No Filter, No Internet JarvesExplainsBuild Your Own UNCENSORED AI Running Completely Offline channel unknown
    Hugging Face blog: Uncensor any LLM with abliteration (Jun 2024) web
  • The research behind itFrom the web

    Arditi and colleagues (2024) found that in 13 open chat models, up to 72 billion parameters, refusal is controlled by a single direction inside the model. Erasing it stops refusals; adding it makes the model refuse even harmless requests. The authors say this shows the brittleness of current safety fine-tuning.

    For you: Background only; useful for understanding why open-weight safety is easy to remove.

    Arditi et al.: Refusal is mediated by a single direction (arXiv) web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • What 'abliteration' isFrom the web

    Abliteration edits a model's weights directly, with no training. Researchers compare the model's internal activity on harmful and harmless prompts, find a 'refusal direction', and remove it, so the model stops refusing. Maxime Labonne's June 2024 Hugging Face post made the method widely known.

    Watch out: The same post says the technique shows how fragile safety training is and raises ethical questions.

    Hugging Face blog: Uncensor any LLM with abliteration (Jun 2024) web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Why people run them offline

    Both videos stress privacy as the draw: the model runs on your own computer, works with the Wi-Fi off, and your data is not sent to any company. One presenter frames it as a fallback for when the internet is down.

    OllamaLM Studio

    For you: The privacy angle fits Mantis's walled-off private lane, but an uncensored model is a different and riskier thing from a private one.

    Private & UNCENSORED Local AI Model | No Filter, No Internet JarvesExplainsBuild Your Own UNCENSORED AI Running Completely Offline channel unknown

  • Quebec parish and civil records at BAnQFrom the web

    BAnQ (Quebec's national library and archives) keeps Quebec's baptism, marriage and burial registers from 1621 up to 100 years ago; newer ones stay with Quebec's civil registrar. Many are scanned on BAnQ numérique: pick 'Registres de l'état civil', choose a parish, then a year, and read the index and register pages in the viewer. BAnQ's search guide describes this with no fee or account mentioned; the fees BAnQ lists are for certified copies ($55 for Quebec residents, $350 for others).

    1. Open BAnQ numérique and choose 'Registres de l'état civil'.
    2. Search the parish name; try other spellings if it is missing.
    3. Open the year, check the index for the act number, then the register.
    4. Remember each folio has a front and back page.
    5. For gaps, search the 'CE' reference in Advitam or ask a BAnQ archivist.

    For you: For the George Cooper research: Cerebra searches, Agent 99 fact-checks, and every fact keeps its BAnQ link. Pages are in French.

    Watch out: Records newer than about 100 years are not at BAnQ, and some registers are not scanned yet. Certified copies currently have long delays.

VVibe coding

Vibe coding means building software by describing what you want to an AI. This tab covers the tools the videos name, the habits that make it work, and the mistakes presenters warn about.

From your videos: 38 of the 105 videos feed this tab, but most only name tools in passing. The habits come mainly from Nate Herk, Simon Scrapes, Sharbel A., Jason Lee and Julian Goldie. 12 entries from the web add the official Anthropic and OpenAI guides, the vibe coding definition and security research on AI-built apps (marked From the web).

Common mistakes 8, A to Z

  • Anthropic's five failure patternsFrom the web

    Anthropic names five common mistakes: the kitchen-sink session that mixes unrelated tasks, correcting over and over, a CLAUDE.md so long that rules get lost, trusting code that looks right but misses edge cases, and open-ended 'investigate' requests that read hundreds of files. The fixes: /clear, a fresh prompt, prune CLAUDE.md, always verify, and scope the search or use subagents.

    CLAUDE.md/clear (Claude Code)

    Watch out: Anthropic's own words: 'If you can't verify it, don't ship it.'

  • A one-line prompt for a big build

    Sharbel A. calls 'Build me an app, make no mistake' a bad prompt: it leaves too much undefined. Big jobs need a designed goal with success criteria and a way to check the result.

Official guides (from the web) 7, A to Z

  • Explore, plan, build, commitFrom the web

    Anthropic suggests four phases for bigger changes: read the code in plan mode, write a plan, build it, then commit. For a large feature, have Claude interview you and write SPEC.md, then build it in a fresh session. Skip the plan when you could describe the change in one sentence.

    1. Press Shift+Tab until plan mode is on.
    2. Ask it to read the relevant files and make a plan.
    3. Press Ctrl+G to edit the plan yourself.
    4. Approve the plan, let it build and test.
    5. Ask it to commit with a clear message.
    Plan modeClaude Code
    Claude Code docs: Best practices web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Give the agent a check it can runFrom the web

    Anthropic's top tip: Claude stops when work looks done, so give it a test, a build or a screenshot to compare that says pass or fail. Then it can fix and re-check alone. Ask for evidence, such as the test output, not just 'it works'.

    1. Put example inputs and expected results in the prompt.
    2. Say 'run the tests after, and fix any failures'.
    3. For screens, paste the design and ask it to screenshot and compare.
    4. Ask it to show the command it ran and the result.
    Claude CodeClaude Code /goalClaude Code hooks

    For you: Matches Chris's rule to check things before reporting them.

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Have a second session review the workFrom the web

    A fresh session or subagent (a helper agent with its own memory) reviews better because it did not write the code. Anthropic shows a Writer and Reviewer pattern and an adversarial review step where a subagent checks the diff. Tell the reviewer to flag only real correctness gaps, because chasing every finding leads to over-engineering.

    1. Finish the change in session A.
    2. Ask a subagent or session B to review the diff against the plan.
    3. Give the findings back to session A to fix.
    Claude Code

    For you: The same idea as Sentinel reviewing Cyborg's work.

    Claude Code docs: Best practices web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • OpenAI's Codex guide in briefFrom the web

    OpenAI says each prompt should give a goal, context, constraints and a 'done when' line. Keep a short, accurate AGENTS.md with run, test and lint commands. Keep one chat per coherent unit of work, and use git worktrees when parallel threads touch the same files.

    1. Write the goal, context, constraints and 'done when'.
    2. Run /init to start AGENTS.md, then trim it.
    3. Use Plan mode for difficult jobs.
    4. Use /review to check a diff.
    CodexAGENTS.mdGit worktrees for parallel agents

    Watch out: OpenAI lists scheduling a recurring task before it is reliable by hand as a common mistake.

  • Start over after two failed correctionsFrom the web

    If you have corrected Claude twice on the same thing, the chat is full of failed attempts. Anthropic says to clear it and start again with a better prompt that uses what you learned. A clean session with a better prompt almost always does better.

    1. Press Esc to stop it mid-task.
    2. Press Esc twice or run /rewind to pick a checkpoint and restore or summarise from there.
    3. Run /clear between unrelated tasks.
    4. Write a new, sharper first prompt.
    /clear (Claude Code)

    Watch out: Checkpoints only undo Claude's own file edits, not changes made by commands. They do not replace git.

    Claude Code docs: Best practices web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Start with tight permissionsFrom the web

    Both Anthropic and OpenAI say to start with tight approval and sandbox settings and loosen them only when needed. Claude Code lets you pre-approve safe commands, run commands in a sandbox (a walled-off area), or use auto mode, where a separate model blocks risky actions. OpenAI lists giving full machine access too early as a common mistake.

    1. Use /permissions to allow only commands you trust.
    2. Use /sandbox so commands run with limited file and network access.
    3. Loosen settings only after the workflow works.

  • Vibe coding versus vibe engineeringFrom the web

    Andrej Karpathy coined 'vibe coding' in a post on X on 2 Feb 2025, meaning accepting AI changes without reading them, for throwaway weekend projects. Simon Willison says it is only vibe coding when you do not review the code; he will not commit code he could not explain to someone else. He calls the careful, accountable version 'vibe engineering', which leans on tests, plans, docs, git and code review.

    1. Vibe code only low-stakes projects.
    2. Keep API keys and private data out.
    3. Set spending limits on paid APIs.
    4. Get an experienced review before sharing widely.

Security of vibe-coded apps (from the web) 4, A to Z

  • AI code often fails security testsFrom the web

    Veracode tested 100+ models in 2025 and across 80 coding tasks found security flaws in 45% of cases; models failed to block cross-site scripting (a common web attack) in 86% of cases. Its 2026 report says things barely moved: an average security pass rate of 56%, even though the code nearly always runs.

    1. Assume AI code is insecure until checked.
    2. Ask for security rules in the prompt.
    3. Run a security review before launch.
    Claude Security

    For you: A clear case for Sentinel reviewing every build Cyborg makes.

    Veracode: 2025 GenAI code security press release webSD Times: Veracode 2026 report web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Made-up package names (slopsquatting)From the web

    Researchers found 19.7% of packages suggested by code models did not exist; when 500 such prompts were rerun 10 times, 43% of the fake names came back every time. Attackers can register those names with malware inside. Open-source models made this mistake far more often (21.7% on average) than commercial ones (5.2%).

    1. Check every new package exists and is the well-known one.
    2. Look at its owner, age and downloads.
    3. Have Sentinel approve new packages.
    CSO Online: AI hallucinations lead to slopsquatting web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • Real case: Lovable apps with open databasesFrom the web

    CVE-2025-48757 (a public security record) covers sites built with Lovable up to 15 Apr 2025. Weak database rules let strangers read or change data without logging in. Lovable disputes the record and says each customer must protect their own data.

    1. Turn on Row Level Security on every table.
    2. Log in as a test user and try to read someone else's data.
    LovableSupabase

    Watch out: A prompt-to-app builder does not make the database safe for you.

    SentinelOne: CVE-2025-48757 web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026

  • The lethal trifecta for agentsFrom the web

    Simon Willison warns about agents that have three things at once: your private data, contact with untrusted content, and a way to send data out. An attacker can then trick the agent into leaking your data. He says the only safe fix is to avoid that combination, not to trust prompts or guardrail products.

    For you: Worth checking for each Hermes agent: does any one of them hold all three?

    Watch out: He says a guard that stops '95% of attacks' is a failing grade in web security.

    Simon Willison: The lethal trifecta web

    Checked 26 Oct 2026
